models.name: Muse Spark Open 816B-A42B
models.parameters: 816B total / 42B active (MoE, 256 experts, top-8 routing; + 1.8B Perception Encoder); HF safetensors total 822,036,529,664
models._note: Open-weights version of Muse Spark with additional safety post-training. Architecture: 62 layers, hidden 8192, 128 Q / 16 KV heads (GQA), head dim 64, gated attention + QK-norm, vocab 202,048, Perception Encoder 1.8B/50 layers. Checkpoints: BF16 (~1.6 TB) and NVFP4 (meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4, ~530 GB, experts-only quantized; 4x Blackwell Ultra or 8x H200); card: needs >=700GB VRAM for NVFP4, 2TB for BF16; runs on two Mac Studios M5 Ultra 512GB via MLX. Partner builds: AMD FP8/MXFP4 (Quark), Intel MXFP4/INT4, speculative drafters DFlash V2 (SGLang, RadixArk) and DSpark (vLLM). Recommended sampling temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0, top_k disabled. Unsloth Dynamic 3.0 GGUFs (unsloth/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-GGUF, quant-only builds, not separately benchmarked): HF sizes UD-IQ1_S 176GB, UD-IQ1_M 209GB, UD-IQ2_XXS 226GB, UD-IQ2_S 275GB, UD-Q2_K_XL 311GB, UD-IQ3_XXS 340GB, UD-Q3_K_XL 401GB, UD-Q4_K_XL 506GB; Unsloth memory guide 1-bit 180-212GB, 2-bit 250-316GB, 3-bit 346-410GB, 4-bit 512GB, 6-bit 640GB, 8-bit 870-950GB (RAM+VRAM); BF16 LM weights ~1.63TB; 2-bit fits 256GB, recommended start Dynamic 2-bit; UD-IQ2_S recommended minimum for agentic tasks (KLD/top-1% charts are images only, no numbers extracted); llama.cpp PR #30616 required. All benchmark scores below at reasoning_effort=xhigh. Registered in S307.

benchmarks.name: CJ-Bench General — accuracy
benchmarks.description: CJ-Bench (Chinese-Jev Benchmark, arXiv 2609.36965, Fudan/NUS/UCAS): Chinese decision benchmark built from held-out test partitions of the Chinese-Jev corpora; General (100,000 decisions, 8 task categories, ~equal choice/noul/score budgets), Medical (200,000), Legal (4,300), Finance (3,600). All models get the same context and candidates. ACC: agreement of top-probability candidate with gold; ECE: 15 equal-width bins; latency: median end-to-end ms per decision on one H200 at batch 1 (hosted Jev API latency includes network RTT). Project page https://gulucaptain.github.io/Chinese-Jev/. Component: general.

benchmarks.name: Ordinal-scale bias panel (40 datasets) — Ordinal (36) accuracy
benchmarks.description: Table 1 main panel macro-average: Ordinal (36) accuracy. Gao et al. (Jilin Univ.), 'More Choices, Fewer Decisions: Ordinal-Scale Bias in JEV-like Direct-Decision Models', arXiv:2609.38827. 40-dataset panel (36 ordinal, 4 nominal: SNIPS, Yahoo Answers, SCOTUS, DBpedia), 5,000 label-stratified items each (200,000 queries/model); measures ordinal scale-utilization bias. DR = 100*(exp(H(pred))/exp(H(gold)) - 1) absolute effective-support deviation (pp, lower better); TVD between predicted and gold label distributions; Uarg/Usoft utilization; nMAE; QWK. Licenses per dataset (Table 5).

benchmarks.name: DecisionRobust — text perturbation — clean acc
benchmarks.description: DecisionRobust (arXiv 2610.19118, Penn State; yifan-lan.github.io/DecisionRobust): adversarial-robustness benchmark for JEV-style decision models built from application tasks (content filtering, tool/skill routing, workflow assessment, retrieval relevance, GUI targeting, physical state, market forecasting, visual decisions, SST-2/MMLU diagnostics) in native Choice/Noul/Score formats; candidates curated via external label-consistency checks and cross-model selection (Jev-1.13.0 construction model).
